9d946b6123a6.en: Three post-mortems. <bookmark mark='a'/> In February 2017 an engineer at Amazon ran a command to take a few servers out of the billing system of its storage service, S3. One input was mistyped. The command removed far more servers, including two subsystems that every request in the region depended on, and restarting them took hours. Amazon changed the tool to remove capacity slowly, and never below a safe floor. <bookmark mark='b'/> In July 2019 Cloudflare deployed a new firewall rule whose regular expression backtracked catastrophically, the failure Part 12 warned about. Pushed to every machine at once, it drove every processor serving web traffic to one hundred percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> And in July 2024 a content update for CrowdStrike's security sensor made its Windows kernel driver read memory out of bounds. About eight and a half million machines crashed, and would not boot until someone repaired each one by hand. <bookmark mark='d'/> None of these was exotic. Each was a routine change, pushed too far, too fast, with nothing to stop it.
9d946b6123a6.zh: 三份事后复盘。<bookmark mark='a'/>2017年2月，Amazon 的一名工程师运行了一条命令，要从它的存储服务 S3 的计费系统里撤下几台服务器。其中一个输入打错了。这条命令撤下了多得多的服务器，其中包括该区域内每个请求都依赖的两个子系统，而重启它们花了好几个小时。Amazon 修改了这个工具，让它缓慢地移除容量，而且永远不低于一个安全下限。<bookmark mark='b'/>2019年7月，Cloudflare 部署了一条新的防火墙规则，它的正则表达式发生了灾难性的回溯，正是第12部分警告过的那种故障。它被同时推送到每一台机器上，把每一个处理网页流量的处理器都推到了百分之100。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在2024年7月，CrowdStrike 安全传感器的一次内容更新，让它的 Windows 内核驱动程序越界读取内存。大约850万台机器崩溃，而且无法启动，直到有人逐台手工修复。<bookmark mark='d'/>这些都不是什么稀奇的事。每一次都是一项例行变更，推得太远、太快，而没有任何东西拦住它。

18109f33cbba.en: A system is only as good as its worst hour, so reliability is counted in minutes. A year has five hundred and twenty-five thousand, nine hundred and sixty of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ninety-nine percent availability allows about three and a half days of downtime a year. <bookmark mark='b'/> Three nines allows under nine hours. <bookmark mark='c'/> Four nines, under an hour, about four minutes a month. <bookmark mark='d'/> Five nines, about five minutes a year, less than the time it takes to notice a problem. <bookmark mark='e'/> Each nine costs about ten times as much as the last, and this part is about how to buy them: the arithmetic of availability, budgets for failure, defences against overload, and the instruments that tell you what actually happened.
18109f33cbba.zh: 一个系统的好坏取决于它最糟糕的那一小时，所以可靠性是按分钟来计算的。一年有52万5960分钟。<bookmark mark='a'/>百分之99的可用性，每年允许大约三天半的停机时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>三个九允许不到9小时。<bookmark mark='c'/>四个九，不到1小时，大约每月4分钟。<bookmark mark='d'/>五个九，每年大约5分钟，比发现一个问题所需的时间还短。<bookmark mark='e'/>每多一个九，花费大约是前一个的10倍，而这一部分讲的就是如何买到它们：可用性的算术、为失败准备的预算、对抗过载的防御，以及告诉你究竟发生了什么的各种仪器。

dbe251b3e1e0.en: This is Part 50 of Computer Science, Built. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will compose availability in series and in parallel; turn reliability into an error budget and derive the alerts that guard it; watch retries melt a system and jitter rescue it; build breakers, bulkheads and load shedding; measure with metrics, traces and profiles that do not lie; learn how incidents are run and studied; and break the Job's own service on purpose, to see what it survives.
dbe251b3e1e0.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第50部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会把可用性串联和并联地组合起来；把可靠性变成错误预算，并推导出守护它的告警；看着重试压垮一个系统，又看着抖动把它救回来；构建断路器、舱壁和负载削减；用不会说谎的指标、追踪和剖析数据来测量；了解事故是怎样处理和研究的；最后故意破坏那项任务自己的服务，看看它能扛过什么。

d88d370450eb.en: Chapter one. The arithmetic of availability.

2bc30618f316.en: Availability is the fraction of time a service does its job. Engineers count it in nines: <bookmark mark='a'/> the number of nines is minus the logarithm, base ten, of the unavailability, and the unavailability times a period is the downtime that period allows. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two nines allows three and a half days a year; three nines, about forty-three minutes a month; <bookmark mark='c'/> four nines, four minutes a month, or one minute a week. <bookmark mark='d'/> Think of it as a budget rather than a promise. At four nines, a bad deploy that takes ten minutes to roll back spends more than two months of it at once.
2bc30618f316.zh: 可用性是一个服务正常工作的时间所占的比例。工程师用几个九来计算它：<bookmark mark='a'/>九的个数，是不可用率以10为底的对数的相反数，而不可用率乘以一段时间，就是这段时间允许的停机时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个九，每年允许三天半；三个九，每月大约43分钟；<bookmark mark='c'/>四个九，每月4分钟，或者每周1分钟。<bookmark mark='d'/>把它看作一份预算，而不是一个承诺。在四个九下，一次需要10分钟才能回滚的糟糕部署，一下子就花掉了两个多月的预算。

ba806f6197d8.en: Part 3's switch circuits show how the parts combine. Let a closed switch mean a part that is up, and a lit lamp mean the service works. <bookmark mark='a'/> In series, current needs every switch, so one part down takes the service down. If failures are independent, the probability that all are up is the product of their availabilities. Ten parts at ninety-nine percent give ninety percent; fifty give sixty. <bookmark mark='b'/> In parallel, the service is down only if every part is down, so multiply the unavailabilities instead. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two parts at ninety-nine percent give four nines; three give six. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a rule of thumb: in series the downtimes add, and in parallel the nines add.
ba806f6197d8.zh: 第3部分的开关电路展示了各个部件如何组合。让一个闭合的开关表示一个正常运行的部件，让一盏亮着的灯表示服务正常。<bookmark mark='a'/>串联时，电流需要经过每一个开关，所以一个部件宕机，服务就宕机。如果故障相互独立，所有部件都正常的概率，就是它们可用性的乘积。10个百分之99的部件给出百分之90；50个给出百分之60。<bookmark mark='b'/>并联时，只有每个部件都宕机，服务才会宕机，所以改为把不可用率相乘。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个百分之99的部件给出四个九；三个给出六个九。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以有一条经验法则：串联时停机时间相加，并联时九的个数相加。

9267ed34bcaf.en: Real systems are both at once. <bookmark mark='a'/> A request passes through name servers, then a load balancer, then an application server, then the database: four stages in series. Replicate each stage, and it becomes a parallel bank worth six nines or more. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now the series law adds three parts in a million: five and a half nines, under two minutes a year. <bookmark mark='c'/> Build the same path from one of each and it reaches only ninety-eight point seven percent, almost five days a year, dominated by its weakest part, the single application server. <bookmark mark='d'/> Replication buys the nines, but every one of these figures assumes the parts fail independently.
9267ed34bcaf.zh: 真实的系统同时是两者。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个请求先经过域名服务器，然后是负载均衡器，然后是应用服务器，最后是数据库：四级串联。把每一级都复制，它就变成一个价值六个九甚至更多的并联组。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在串联定律加上了百万分之三：五个半九，每年不到2分钟。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果同样的路径每一级只用一个部件来搭，它只能达到百分之98.7，每年将近5天，主要由它最弱的部件决定，也就是那台唯一的应用服务器。<bookmark mark='d'/>复制买来了这些九，但这里的每一个数字，都假定各个部件的故障相互独立。

af1d85bf2c76.en: Where does a part's availability come from? <bookmark mark='a'/> A part runs for a while, fails, is repaired, and runs again. Here is one simulated server's year: up for random stretches averaging a month, seven hundred and twenty hours, then down for repairs averaging two hours. <bookmark mark='b'/> Over a long run the fraction of time up is the mean time between failures over that plus the mean time to repair: ninety-nine point seven two percent, which two hundred simulated years confirm. <bookmark mark='c'/> The formula has two levers, and they are worth exactly the same: failing half as often and repairing twice as fast both halve the downtime. <bookmark mark='d'/> Repair is usually the cheaper one: failing over in ten minutes is worth twelve times fewer failures.
af1d85bf2c76.zh: 一个部件的可用性从何而来？<bookmark mark='a'/>一个部件运行一段时间，发生故障，被修复，再次运行。这是一台模拟服务器的一年：正常运行的时段长短随机，平均一个月，也就是720小时，然后停机修复，平均2小时。<bookmark mark='b'/>在长期运行中，正常运行时间所占的比例，是平均故障间隔时间，除以它与平均修复时间之和：百分之99.72，200个模拟的年份证实了这一点。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个公式有两根杠杆，而它们的价值完全相同：故障次数减半，和修复速度加倍，都会让停机时间减半。<bookmark mark='d'/>修复通常是更便宜的那一根：在10分钟内完成故障转移，相当于让故障次数减少到十二分之一。

d98ff5b454ed.en: <bookmark mark='a'/> Three replicas at ninety-nine point nine percent each promise nine nines, if they fail independently. <bookmark mark='b'/> But suppose a share of each replica's downtime has a common cause: a bad deploy, one power feed, one configuration file. That cause is a switch in series with the whole bank, and when it opens, every replica is down together. <bookmark mark='c'/> If just one percent of the downtime is shared, the three give five nines, not nine. At ten percent, four; at thirty percent, three and a half. <bookmark mark='d'/> The common part caps the whole at its own availability. The three post-mortems that opened this part were all of this kind: one change, applied everywhere at once.
d98ff5b454ed.zh: <bookmark mark='a'/>3个副本，每个百分之99.9，如果它们的故障相互独立，就能承诺九个九。<bookmark mark='b'/>但假设每个副本的停机时间中，有一部分有一个共同原因：一次糟糕的部署、同一路供电、同一个配置文件。这个原因就是一个与整组副本串联的开关，当它断开时，每个副本都一起宕机。<bookmark mark='c'/>只要停机时间中有百分之1是共享的，这3个副本就只能给出五个九，而不是九个。百分之10时，四个九；百分之30时，三个半九。<bookmark mark='d'/>共同的部分把整体的可用性封顶在它自己的可用性上。开启这一部分的那三份事后复盘，全都属于这一类：一项变更，同时应用到所有地方。

0217f071c21c.en: Chapter two. Objectives, and the budget for failing to meet them.
0217f071c21c.zh: 第二章：目标，以及为未能达到目标准备的预算。

7eda7d08ee0f.en: Reliability needs three words. <bookmark mark='a'/> An indicator, the SLI, is something measured: of the valid requests, the fraction that were good, say answered correctly within three hundred milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> An objective, the SLO, is the target for that indicator over a window: here ninety-nine point nine percent over thirty days. It is an engineering choice, and it should be what users actually notice. <bookmark mark='c'/> An agreement, the SLA, is a contract with consequences, refunds when it is broken, and so it is set looser than the objective. <bookmark mark='d'/> In our synthetic month the indicator came in at ninety-nine point nine four five percent. It met the objective, and the gap between the objective and perfection is not waste. It is room to change things.
7eda7d08ee0f.zh: 可靠性需要三个词。<bookmark mark='a'/>指标，也就是服务级指标（SLI），是测量出来的东西：在有效的请求中，良好请求所占的比例，比如在300毫秒内得到正确回答的请求。<bookmark mark='b'/>目标，也就是服务级目标（SLO），是这个指标在一个时间窗口内要达到的目标值：这里是30天内百分之99.9。它是一个工程上的选择，应当是用户真正会注意到的东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>协议，也就是服务级协议（SLA），是一份带有后果的合同，违约时要退款，所以它定得比目标更宽松。<bookmark mark='d'/>在我们合成的一个月里，这个指标达到了百分之99.945。它达到了目标，而目标与完美之间的差距并不是浪费。它是做出改变的空间。

df98a065b0e1.en: The objective turns into a resource. <bookmark mark='a'/> The error budget is the unreliability the objective allows: one bad request in a thousand, or the equivalent of forty-three minutes of total outage a month. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is our synthetic month, spending it. Background errors trickle steadily. On day eight, a twenty-five minute outage at a quarter of requests takes fourteen and a half percent in one bite. On day fourteen a six-hour degradation takes ten percent. From day twenty a slow leak, only two errors in a thousand, quietly takes almost nineteen percent over three days. <bookmark mark='c'/> The month ends with fifty-five percent spent. <bookmark mark='d'/> The budget is the contract between the people who ship features and the people who carry the pager: while budget remains, ship; when it is gone, freeze risky launches and spend the effort on reliability.
df98a065b0e1.zh: 目标变成了一种资源。<bookmark mark='a'/>错误预算就是目标所允许的不可靠程度：每1000个请求中有1个坏请求，或者相当于每月43分钟的完全中断。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是我们合成的那个月，正在花掉它。背景错误稳定地一点点流出。第8天，一次影响四分之一请求的25分钟中断，一口就吃掉了百分之14.5。第14天，一次6小时的性能下降吃掉了百分之10。从第20天起，一次缓慢的泄漏，每1000个请求只有2个错误，在3天里悄悄吃掉了将近百分之19。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个月结束时，预算花掉了百分之55。<bookmark mark='d'/>预算是交付功能的人和背着寻呼机值班的人之间的契约：只要预算还有剩余，就发布；预算用完了，就冻结有风险的上线，把精力花在可靠性上。

c82a62f94a82.en: When should the budget wake someone up? <bookmark mark='a'/> Measure the burn rate: the error rate divided by the rate the objective allows. A burn rate of one spends the budget in exactly thirty days; a burn rate of b spends it in thirty days over b. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two lasts fifteen days; six, five days; fourteen point four, just over two days. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now turn it around. To page when a share f of the month's budget has gone within a window w, the threshold is f times seven hundred and twenty hours, over w. <bookmark mark='d'/> The Site Reliability Workbook's choices: two percent in an hour gives fourteen point four, and pages; five percent in six hours gives six, and pages; ten percent in three days gives one, and opens a ticket for working hours.
c82a62f94a82.zh: 预算应该在什么时候把人叫醒？<bookmark mark='a'/>测量消耗速率：错误率除以目标所允许的错误率。消耗速率为1，恰好在30天里花完预算；消耗速率为 b，在30除以 b 天里花完。<bookmark mark='b'/>速率为2，能撑15天；为6，撑5天；为14.4，刚过2天。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在反过来。要想在一个窗口 w 之内花掉一个月预算的一个份额 f 时呼叫值班人员，阈值就是 f 乘以720小时，再除以 w。<bookmark mark='d'/>《站点可靠性工作手册》（The Site Reliability Workbook）的选择是：1小时内百分之2，给出14.4，触发呼叫；6小时内百分之5，给出6，触发呼叫；3天内百分之10，给出1，开一张在工作时间处理的工单。

8a5083153861.en: We scored five alerting rules from the Workbook on this month, counting an incident as worth a page if it costs at least two percent of the budget. <bookmark mark='a'/> Paging whenever the error rate exceeds the objective over ten minutes catches everything at once, and pages twenty times, including for blips that cost half a percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> A thirty-six-hour window is quiet for blips, but slow to notice and slower to stop: it keeps paging for a day and a half after the outage. <bookmark mark='c'/> A single fast burn threshold misses the degradation and the leak entirely. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two burn rates, with a ticket for the slowest, catch all three significant incidents, but the six-hour window keeps the page firing for six hours. <bookmark mark='e'/> The cure is a second, short window that must agree: the alert ends half an hour after the outage does. That last rule is the Workbook's recommendation.
8a5083153861.zh: 我们用这个月给手册中的五条告警规则打了分，把代价至少为预算百分之2的事件，算作值得呼叫的事件。<bookmark mark='a'/>只要10分钟内的错误率超过目标就呼叫，能立刻抓住一切，但会呼叫20次，包括那些只花掉百分之0.5的小波动。<bookmark mark='b'/>36小时的窗口对小波动很安静，但发现得慢，停下来更慢：中断结束后，它还要继续呼叫一天半。<bookmark mark='c'/>单一的快速消耗阈值，完全漏掉了性能下降和泄漏。<bookmark mark='d'/>两个消耗速率，再给最慢的那个配一张工单，能抓住全部三个重大事件，但6小时的窗口会让呼叫持续触发6个小时。<bookmark mark='e'/>解药是再加一个必须同时满足的短窗口：告警在中断结束半小时后就停止。最后这条规则，正是手册的推荐。

1eec876428bc.en: Chapter three. How systems fail, and why some failures outlast their causes.
1eec876428bc.zh: 第三章：系统如何失败，以及为什么有些故障比它们的起因持续得更久。

484428f66183.en: Failures come in kinds, and each kind contains the ones before it. <bookmark mark='a'/> The kindest is fail-stop: a machine halts, and everyone else can tell that it has. Fault-tolerant protocols love it. <bookmark mark='b'/> A plain crash halts without announcing it. Omission loses some messages and not others. <bookmark mark='c'/> A timing failure answers, but too late: a slow disk, a long pause. <bookmark mark='d'/> And an arbitrary failure may do anything at all, even send wrong answers. <bookmark mark='e'/> The failures that hurt most in practice are gray: partial, intermittent, and seen differently by the health check, which reports all is well, and by the users, who are timing out. Chapter fifteen returns to them.
484428f66183.zh: 故障分为几类，每一类都包含它之前的那些。<bookmark mark='a'/>最友好的是失效停止：一台机器停下来，而其他所有人都能知道它停了。容错协议最喜欢它。<bookmark mark='b'/>普通的崩溃会停下来，但不会宣布。遗漏故障丢掉一些消息，而不丢另一些。<bookmark mark='c'/>时序故障会回答，但太晚了：一块慢磁盘，一次长时间的暂停。<bookmark mark='d'/>而任意故障可以做任何事，甚至发送错误的答案。<bookmark mark='e'/>在实践中伤害最大的故障是灰色的：局部的、时有时无的，而且健康检查和用户看到的样子不同，健康检查报告一切正常，用户却在超时。第十五章会回到它们。

d5b002171149.en: Failures spread. <bookmark mark='a'/> Five servers share a load that keeps each one seventy-two percent busy. <bookmark mark='b'/> One fails, and the balancer moves its share to the other four: each is now at ninety percent. The load each survivor carries is the original times n over n minus k. <bookmark mark='c'/> A second one fails, perhaps because ninety percent made it slow enough to fail its health check, and the remaining three are asked for a hundred and twenty percent. <bookmark mark='d'/> They cannot give it. Queues grow, they too look dead, and the cascade takes the rest. <bookmark mark='e'/> The remedies come later in this part: headroom, so that losing machines does not overload the rest, and servers that refuse excess work instead of falling over under it.
d5b002171149.zh: 故障会蔓延。<bookmark mark='a'/>5台服务器分担一份负载，每台百分之72忙碌。<bookmark mark='b'/>一台出了故障，负载均衡器把它的那一份转给其他4台：现在每台百分之90。每台幸存的服务器承担的负载，是原来的负载乘以 n，再除以 n 减 k。<bookmark mark='c'/>第二台出了故障，也许正是因为百分之90让它慢到通不过健康检查，于是剩下的3台被要求承担百分之120。<bookmark mark='d'/>它们给不出来。队列增长，它们看起来也像是死了，级联故障吞没了其余的服务器。<bookmark mark='e'/>补救办法在这一部分的后面：留出余量，让失去机器不会压垮其余的机器；以及让服务器拒绝多余的工作，而不是在它的重压下倒下。

acb601f5b2cf.en: Now the strangest failure of all. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this simulation a server answers a hundred requests a second, and users send eighty: comfortable. Clients give up on a request after one second. <bookmark mark='b'/> At thirty seconds comes a trigger: for ten seconds, capacity halves, as when a replica is lost or a long pause stalls the server. <bookmark mark='c'/> Without retries, a queue builds, requests time out, and eleven seconds after the trigger ends the server has caught up. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now let each client retry a timed-out request up to three times, immediately. The same ten seconds tip it over. The load sent climbs to about 320 requests a second, four times what the users want, <bookmark mark='e'/> and the number answered in time falls to zero, and stays there, eighty seconds after the trigger has gone. Nothing is broken any more. The system is simply stuck.
acb601f5b2cf.zh: 现在来看所有故障中最奇怪的一种。<bookmark mark='a'/>在这个模拟中，一台服务器每秒回答100个请求，而用户每秒发送80个：很宽裕。客户端在1秒后放弃一个请求。<bookmark mark='b'/>在第30秒出现一个触发因素：在10秒钟里，容量减半，就像失去一个副本，或者一次长时间的暂停让服务器停顿时那样。<bookmark mark='c'/>没有重试时，队列积压，请求超时，而在触发因素结束11秒后，服务器就赶上来了。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在让每个客户端对超时的请求立即重试，最多3次。同样的10秒钟就把它推翻了。发出的负载攀升到大约每秒320个请求，是用户需求的4倍，<bookmark mark='e'/>而按时得到回答的请求数降到了零，并且一直停在那里，在触发因素消失80秒之后依然如此。什么都没有坏。这个系统只是卡住了。

2ff0e32c373f.en: Nathan Bronson and colleagues named this a metastable failure, in 2021. <bookmark mark='a'/> A system is stable at low load. At high load it becomes vulnerable: still working, but a trigger can push it into a bad state, <bookmark mark='b'/> and the bad state sustains itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here is the loop. The queue is long, so requests wait past their timeout. Their clients retry, so there is more load than capacity, so the queue stays long. <bookmark mark='d'/> Meanwhile the server is fully busy, with work for clients who have already given up. Removing the trigger does nothing, because the loop no longer needs it; only cutting the load breaks it. <bookmark mark='e'/> Huang and colleagues, in 2022, found this pattern in the incident reports of many large services. The next chapter is about retrying without feeding the loop.
2ff0e32c373f.zh: Nathan Bronson 和同事在2021年把这称为亚稳态故障。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个系统在低负载下是稳定的。在高负载下它变得脆弱：仍在工作，但一个触发因素就能把它推入一个坏状态，<bookmark mark='b'/>而这个坏状态会自我维持。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是那个回路。队列很长，所以请求的等待超过了它们的超时时间。它们的客户端重试，于是负载超过容量，于是队列一直很长。<bookmark mark='d'/>与此同时，服务器忙个不停，做的却是那些客户端早已放弃了的工作。去掉触发因素毫无作用，因为这个回路已经不再需要它；只有削减负载才能打破它。<bookmark mark='e'/>Huang 和同事在2022年，在许多大型服务的事故报告中发现了这种模式。下一章讲的是如何重试，而不去喂养这个回路。

98afedd5aa7a.en: Chapter four. Timeouts, retries, backoff and jitter.
98afedd5aa7a.zh: 第四章：超时、重试、退避与抖动。

2ee3bf91ad36.en: A request that never returns is worse than one that fails. <bookmark mark='a'/> A timeout turns an endless wait into a known failure; set it from the dependency's measured latency, a little above its ninety-nine point nine percentile, and pass the deadline down, so that inner layers stop working for callers who have given up. <bookmark mark='b'/> Failures can be retried. But look what happens when every layer does it. The database is down, and each of three layers tries four times. <bookmark mark='c'/> One tap becomes sixty-four attempts on a database that is already struggling. <bookmark mark='d'/> So retry at one layer only, and only requests that are safe to repeat, with Part 43's idempotency keys.
2ee3bf91ad36.zh: 一个永远不返回的请求，比一个失败的请求更糟。<bookmark mark='a'/>超时把无尽的等待变成一个已知的失败；根据依赖项测得的延迟来设置它，略高于它的第99.9百分位数，并把截止时间向下传递，让内层不再为已经放弃的调用者工作。<bookmark mark='b'/>失败可以重试。但看看每一层都这么做时会发生什么。数据库宕机了，三层中的每一层都尝试4次。<bookmark mark='c'/>一次点击，就变成了对一个本已吃力的数据库的64次尝试。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以只在一层重试，而且只重试那些可以安全重复的请求，用第43部分的幂等键。

dcda1914eaa4.en: Retry immediately, and clients that failed together fail together again. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here twenty clients each need one write to the same record; a write fails if another overlaps it. With no backoff they collide every time, for ever. <bookmark mark='b'/> Exponential backoff, waiting one, two, four, eight units, makes far fewer attempts, but the clients stay in lockstep, wait the same time, and collide again. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add jitter, a random wait between zero and the exponential bound, and the herd spreads out. The white dots are successes: all twenty finish, after a hundred and seventy-five attempts. Randomness breaks the symmetry, as it did for Ethernet in 1976.
dcda1914eaa4.zh: 立即重试，一起失败的客户端就会再一起失败。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有20个客户端，每个都需要对同一条记录做一次写入；如果另一次写入与它重叠，这次写入就失败。没有退避，它们每次都碰撞，永无止境。<bookmark mark='b'/>指数退避，依次等待1、2、4、8个单位，尝试次数少得多，但客户端仍然步调一致，等待同样的时间，又碰撞了。<bookmark mark='c'/>加上抖动，也就是在零和指数上界之间随机等待一段时间，这群客户端就散开了。白点是成功：20个全部完成，用了175次尝试。随机性打破了对称，就像1976年它为以太网做的那样。

bf6e955c7113.en: Marc Brooker compared ways to back off in 2015; we repeat his experiment with a hundred clients. <bookmark mark='a'/> With no backoff, almost a million calls, and the clients never all finish. Plain exponential backoff cuts the calls to under three thousand, but still never finishes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Full jitter waits a random time up to the exponential bound. Equal jitter keeps half the bound and randomizes the rest. Decorrelated jitter grows from the previous wait instead. All three finish, with about a thousand to eighteen hundred calls. <bookmark mark='c'/> Between them the differences are small, and change with the load. The lesson is the one Brooker drew: backoff without jitter is the mistake; any jitter is far better.
bf6e955c7113.zh: Marc Brooker 在2015年比较了几种退避方式；我们用100个客户端重复他的实验。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有退避时，调用将近100万次，而客户端永远无法全部完成。普通的指数退避把调用次数削减到不到3000次，但仍然永远完成不了。<bookmark mark='b'/>完全抖动，随机等待一段不超过指数上界的时间。等量抖动保留上界的一半，把其余部分随机化。去相关抖动则从上一次的等待时间增长。三种都能完成，调用大约1000到1800次。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们之间的差别很小，而且随负载而变。教训正是 Brooker 得出的那个：不带抖动的退避才是错误；任何抖动都要好得多。

c0d5a0d9c85c.en: Back to chapter three's metastable server. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give them exponential backoff with full jitter. It does not help. Backoff spreads the retries out in time, but every timed-out request still makes up to four attempts, and the sent load stays near three hundred a second. The loop holds. <bookmark mark='b'/> What breaks it is limiting the number of retries. With a retry budget, each client may add retries worth at most a tenth of its first attempts, kept as a token bucket like Part 48's rate limiter. <bookmark mark='c'/> The sent load can rise only ten percent above demand, the queue drains, and the server answers again nineteen seconds after the trigger. Google's SRE book recommends the same ten percent.
c0d5a0d9c85c.zh: 回到第三章那台亚稳态的服务器。<bookmark mark='a'/>给它的客户端用上带完全抖动的指数退避。这没有用。退避把重试在时间上分散开，但每个超时的请求仍然最多要尝试4次，发出的负载停留在每秒300个左右。回路依然维持着。<bookmark mark='b'/>打破它的，是限制重试的次数。有了重试预算，每个客户端增加的重试，最多只能相当于它首次尝试的十分之一，用一个令牌桶来记账，就像第48部分的限流器。<bookmark mark='c'/>发出的负载只能比需求高出百分之10，队列排空，服务器在触发因素出现19秒后再次开始回答。Google 的《站点可靠性工程》一书推荐的，也是这同样的百分之10。

6f40fdcb3e76.en: One kind of retry makes things faster. <bookmark mark='a'/> A request goes to server A, which happens to be in a long pause. <bookmark mark='b'/> If no answer has come by a short deadline, send a copy to server B, take whichever answer comes first, and cancel the other. Jeffrey Dean and Luiz Barroso called these hedged requests, in The Tail at Scale: the tail of Part 39. <bookmark mark='c'/> In our simulation, replies are usually quick, but one request in fifty hits a two-hundred-millisecond pause. Without hedging the ninety-ninth percentile is two hundred milliseconds. <bookmark mark='d'/> Hedging at fifty milliseconds cuts it to fifty-three, for two percent more requests; at twenty, to twenty-five, for under four percent. Hedge earlier, and the extra load grows faster than the tail shrinks.
6f40fdcb3e76.zh: 有一种重试能让事情变快。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个请求发往服务器 A，而它恰好处在一次长时间的暂停中。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果在一个很短的期限内还没有回答，就把同样的请求再发一份给服务器 B，采用先到的那个回答，并取消另一个。Jeffrey Dean 和 Luiz Barroso 在《规模下的尾延迟》（The Tail at Scale）中，把这称为对冲请求：也就是第39部分的那个尾部。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们的模拟中，回复通常很快，但每50个请求中有1个会碰上一次200毫秒的暂停。不对冲时，第99百分位数是200毫秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>在50毫秒时对冲，把它降到53毫秒，代价是多出百分之2的请求；在20毫秒时对冲，降到25毫秒，代价不到百分之4。对冲得再早，额外负载的增长就比尾部的缩短更快。

64c53c28a084.en: Chapter five. Breakers, bulkheads, and the art of refusing work.
64c53c28a084.zh: 第五章：断路器、舱壁，以及拒绝工作的艺术。

6660f1d77365.en: Michael Nygard's book Release It!, in 2007, borrowed a device from electricians. <bookmark mark='a'/> A circuit breaker sits in the client, in front of a dependency. Closed, it lets calls through and counts the failures. <bookmark mark='b'/> When most recent calls fail, it trips open: every call fails at once, with no timeout to wait for and no load added to a struggling dependency. <bookmark mark='c'/> After a cool-down it goes half-open and lets a few probe calls through. <bookmark mark='d'/> If they succeed, it closes again; if they fail, it opens again.
6660f1d77365.zh: Michael Nygard 在2007年的书《发布！》（Release It!）里，从电工那里借来了一个装置。<bookmark mark='a'/>断路器（熔断器）位于客户端里，挡在一个依赖项的前面。闭合时，它让调用通过，并统计失败的次数。<bookmark mark='b'/>当最近的调用大多失败时，它跳闸断开：每个调用都立即失败，不用等待任何超时，也不给一个正在挣扎的依赖项增加负载。<bookmark mark='c'/>经过一段冷却时间后，它进入半开状态，放几个试探调用过去。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果它们成功，它就再次闭合；如果它们失败，它就再次断开。

af12518b5476.en: Here is chapter three's server again, its clients retrying three times. <bookmark mark='a'/> Without a breaker, the retries hold it in the bad state for good. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now give every client a breaker. Two seconds into the trigger most calls are failing, the breakers open, and the load sent falls almost to nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> The server drains its queue, the probes succeed, the breakers close, and the server is answering at full rate as the trigger ends. <bookmark mark='d'/> In all, nine thousand one hundred and ten answers in time, against two thousand five hundred and sixty-seven.
af12518b5476.zh: 又是第三章的那台服务器，它的客户端会重试3次。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有断路器时，重试把它永远困在坏状态里。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在给每个客户端一个断路器。触发因素开始2秒后，大多数调用都在失败，断路器断开，发出的负载几乎降到了零。<bookmark mark='c'/>服务器排空它的队列，试探调用成功，断路器闭合，而在触发因素结束时，服务器已经在以全速回答了。<bookmark mark='d'/>总共有9110个请求按时得到回答，而没有断路器时是2567个。

840d7312c3af.en: The server can defend itself too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Before serving a request, it checks how long the request has waited, and drops it if that is over half a second, since its client is about to give up. A rejection costs a fiftieth of an answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> Through the trigger it sheds what it cannot serve in time, answers the rest at its reduced capacity, and afterwards recovers at once. <bookmark mark='c'/> This is CoDel's idea from Part 37, moved from routers to services: judge a queue by how long its requests have waited, not by its length. Ben Maurer described Facebook's servers doing this in 2015, switching to last in, first out when the queue is long, so that the newest requests are served first.
840d7312c3af.zh: 服务器也能保护自己。<bookmark mark='a'/>在处理一个请求之前，它检查这个请求已经等了多久，如果超过半秒就丢弃它，因为它的客户端马上就要放弃了。一次拒绝的代价，是一次回答的五十分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>在整个触发期间，它削减掉那些无法按时处理的请求，以它降低了的容量回答其余的请求，之后立刻恢复。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是第37部分里 CoDel 的思想，从路由器搬到了服务上：根据一个队列里的请求已经等了多久来判断它，而不是根据它的长度。Ben Maurer 在2015年描述了 Facebook 的服务器这样做，在队列很长时切换成后进先出，让最新的请求先得到处理。

823a9e827c1f.en: Put the six side by side. <bookmark mark='a'/> Users sent eighty requests a second for two minutes. Immediate retries, with or without backoff, answered just over a quarter of them; the retry budget recovered after nineteen seconds, and no retries at all after eleven. <bookmark mark='b'/> Shedding and the breakers never got stuck. <bookmark mark='c'/> What works is reducing the load, at the server or at the client, and real systems combine all three.
823a9e827c1f.zh: 把这六种做法放在一起比较。<bookmark mark='a'/>用户在两分钟里每秒发送80个请求。立即重试，无论有没有退避，都只回答了其中略多于四分之一；重试预算在19秒后恢复，而完全不重试在11秒后恢复。<bookmark mark='b'/>负载削减和断路器从来没有卡住。<bookmark mark='c'/>有效的做法是降低负载，无论在服务器端还是在客户端，而真实的系统会把这三种结合起来。

4246fbb72540.en: A ship's hull is divided by bulkheads, so that one leak floods one compartment, not the ship. <bookmark mark='a'/> A service calls A forty times a second and B twenty, from one pool of thirty threads; a call that finds no free thread is rejected. <bookmark mark='b'/> At twenty seconds B turns slow, two seconds a call instead of fifty milliseconds, and its calls fill the pool. <bookmark mark='c'/> So calls to the healthy A fail too: in the worst second, only twenty-eight percent succeed. <bookmark mark='d'/> Split the pool into two bulkheads of fifteen, and A does not notice. B, with half the threads, does worse. The damage stays where it started.
4246fbb72540.zh: 船体被舱壁分隔开，这样一处漏水只淹没一个隔舱，而不是整条船。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个服务每秒调用 A 40次、调用 B 20次，共用一个30个线程的池；找不到空闲线程的调用会被拒绝。<bookmark mark='b'/>在第20秒，B 变慢了，每次调用2秒，而不是50毫秒，它的调用占满了线程池。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是对健康的 A 的调用也失败了：在最糟的那一秒，只有百分之28成功。<bookmark mark='d'/>把线程池分成两个各有15个线程的舱壁，A 就毫无察觉。B 只有一半的线程，情况更糟。损害留在了它开始的地方。

a34168ec475d.en: Serving something less is better than refusing. <bookmark mark='a'/> A product page has parts that matter unequally. When the recommender is slow, the page neither waits nor fails: it shows a cached list of popular items, and the price and the buy button still work. <bookmark mark='b'/> Overload can also be pushed back to its source: Part 43's backpressure bounds every queue, so a full queue slows the producer instead of growing. <bookmark mark='c'/> And when something must be refused, refuse the least important first. Google's SRE book describes tagging each request with a criticality, from critical plus down to sheddable, and shedding from the bottom.
a34168ec475d.zh: 提供少一点的东西，好过拒绝。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个商品页面的各个部分重要性不同。当推荐系统变慢时，页面既不等待也不失败：它显示一份缓存的热门商品列表，而价格和购买按钮照常工作。<bookmark mark='b'/>过载也可以被推回它的源头：第43部分的背压给每个队列设上界，所以一个满了的队列会让生产者放慢，而不是继续增长。<bookmark mark='c'/>而当某些东西必须被拒绝时，先拒绝最不重要的。Google 的《站点可靠性工程》一书描述了给每个请求标上一个关键度，从“最关键”（critical plus）一直到“可丢弃”（sheddable），并从最低的一级开始削减。

391e9c016429.en: Chapter six. Redundancy: how many spares, and where to put them.
391e9c016429.zh: 第六章：冗余：备用要多少，放在哪里。

15a9870e84f1.en: Redundancy starts with counting. <bookmark mark='a'/> A service needs the capacity of ten machines, and each machine is up ninety-nine percent of the time, independently. With exactly ten, the service is whole only when all ten are up: ninety percent of the time, about one nine. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add one spare, N plus one, and it survives any single failure: two point three nines. <bookmark mark='c'/> But machines are also taken out on purpose, for deploys and maintenance, and a failure during that window finds no spare. So the usual rule is N plus two, three point seven nines here. <bookmark mark='d'/> Jim Gray's 1985 study of Tandem's fault-tolerant computers found that operations and software, not hardware, caused most of their outages. Plan for the machine you take out yourself.
15a9870e84f1.zh: 冗余从计数开始。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个服务需要10台机器的容量，而每台机器有百分之99的时间正常运行，彼此独立。如果恰好只有10台，那么只有当10台全部正常时，服务才是完整的：百分之90的时间，大约一个九。<bookmark mark='b'/>加上一台备用，也就是 N+1，它就能扛过任何单个故障：2.3个九。<bookmark mark='c'/>但机器也会被有意撤下，用于部署和维护，而在那段时间里发生的故障，就找不到备用了。所以通常的规则是 N+2，在这里是3.7个九。<bookmark mark='d'/>Jim Gray 在1985年对 Tandem 容错计算机的研究发现，造成它们大多数中断的是运维和软件，而不是硬件。要为你自己撤下的那台机器做好计划。

29547b02b800.en: There are two ways to keep a spare. <bookmark mark='a'/> Active-passive: a primary serves, and a standby follows its log, ready to take over. <bookmark mark='b'/> When the primary dies, something must notice and promote the standby, and that time is downtime, chapter one's repair time. Worse, the standby has never served real traffic, so failover is the least tested path in the system. <bookmark mark='c'/> Active-active: every copy serves all the time, so failover is only routing, exercised every day. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price is headroom. To lose one of n sites, each must run below n minus one over n of its capacity: a half for two sites, two thirds for three. It is chapter three's cascade arithmetic, run in reverse.
29547b02b800.zh: 保留备用有两种方式。<bookmark mark='a'/>主备（active-passive）：一个主节点提供服务，一个备节点跟随它的日志，随时准备接管。<bookmark mark='b'/>当主节点死掉时，必须有什么东西注意到，并提升备节点，而这段时间就是停机时间，也就是第一章的修复时间。更糟的是，备节点从来没有处理过真实的流量，所以故障转移是系统里测试得最少的路径。<bookmark mark='c'/>多活（active-active）：每一份副本始终都在提供服务，所以故障转移只是路由，每天都在演练。<bookmark mark='d'/>代价是余量。要能失去 n 个站点中的一个，每个站点的负载都必须低于它容量的 n 减1除以 n：两个站点是一半，三个站点是三分之二。这正是第三章的级联算术，反过来运行。

cadf932b83a2.en: The largest unit of redundancy is a whole region, a separate set of buildings, power and network, because, as chapter one showed, replicas that share a cause fail together. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three regions share the traffic, each sixty percent busy. <bookmark mark='b'/> Region two starts to misbehave: errors are rising, and nobody yet knows why. <bookmark mark='c'/> The first move is not to debug but to evacuate: steer its traffic to the other two, which rise to ninety percent. Debug afterwards, with no users waiting. <bookmark mark='d'/> Evacuation needs three things ready in advance: headroom in the other regions; the data, already there through Part 39's replication, since whatever had not been copied is lost or stranded; and practice, because an evacuation that has never been rehearsed is a hope, not a plan.
cadf932b83a2.zh: 最大的冗余单位是一整个区域，也就是一组独立的建筑、电力和网络，因为正如第一章所示，共享同一个原因的副本会一起失败。<bookmark mark='a'/>三个区域分担流量，每个百分之60忙碌。<bookmark mark='b'/>区域2开始出问题：错误在上升，而且还没有人知道为什么。<bookmark mark='c'/>第一步不是调试，而是撤离：把它的流量引到另外两个区域，它们升到百分之90。之后再调试，那时已经没有用户在等待。<bookmark mark='d'/>撤离需要提前准备好三样东西：其他区域里的余量；数据，已经通过第39部分的复制放在了那里，因为任何尚未复制过去的东西都会丢失或被困住；还有演练，因为一次从未排练过的撤离只是一个希望，而不是一个计划。

204a9b8b2d63.en: Finally, a group that agrees. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 38's Raft serves while a majority of its nodes is up, because every decision needs a majority of votes. Five nodes survive two failures; <bookmark mark='b'/> a third failure takes the majority, and with it the service, though nothing committed is lost. <bookmark mark='c'/> If nodes fail independently, the group's availability is the chance that more than half are up, a sum over the binomial distribution. <bookmark mark='d'/> At ninety-nine percent a node, three nodes give three and a half nines, five give five, and seven give six and a half. At ninety-nine point nine, five nodes give eight. <bookmark mark='e'/> Two caveats. Even sizes buy nothing: four nodes survive one failure, like three. And the nines assume independence; chapter one showed how a shared cause caps them, which is why the five nodes go in different zones.
204a9b8b2d63.zh: 最后，一个达成一致的群组。<bookmark mark='a'/>第38部分的 Raft，只要它的大多数节点正常就能提供服务，因为每个决定都需要多数票。5个节点能扛过两个故障；<bookmark mark='b'/>第三个故障就会失去多数派，服务也随之失去，不过已提交的东西一样都不会丢。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果节点的故障相互独立，这个群组的可用性就是超过一半节点正常的概率，也就是二项分布上的一个求和。<bookmark mark='d'/>每个节点百分之99时，3个节点给出三个半九，5个给出五个九，7个给出六个半九。每个节点百分之99.9时，5个节点给出八个九。<bookmark mark='e'/>两点提醒。偶数规模买不到任何东西：4个节点只能扛过一个故障，和3个一样。而这些九假定了独立性；第一章展示了共同原因如何给它们封顶，这就是为什么这5个节点要放在不同的可用区里。

9e1f76bb466c.en: Chapter seven. Metrics, and why averages lie.
9e1f76bb466c.zh: 第七章：指标，以及平均值为什么会说谎。

e63462f18ebd.en: Prometheus, begun at SoundCloud in 2012, stores three kinds of metric. <bookmark mark='a'/> A counter only goes up: requests, errors, bytes. You chart its rate, which survives a missed reading and a restart that resets it. <bookmark mark='b'/> A gauge goes up and down: queue length, memory in use. <bookmark mark='c'/> A histogram counts observations into buckets: under ten milliseconds, under twenty-five, under fifty. Buckets add, across servers and across time, and that turns out to matter.
e63462f18ebd.zh: Prometheus 于2012年在 SoundCloud 起步，它存储三种指标。<bookmark mark='a'/>计数器只增不减：请求、错误、字节。你画出的是它的速率，这能扛过一次漏掉的读数，也能扛过一次把它清零的重启。<bookmark mark='b'/>计量器（gauge）可增可减：队列长度、正在使用的内存。<bookmark mark='c'/>直方图把观测值计入各个桶：小于10毫秒、小于25毫秒、小于50毫秒。桶可以相加，跨服务器，也跨时间，而这一点后来证明很重要。

145088f8ee45.en: Here are two hundred thousand simulated latencies, on logarithmic axes. Most take about twenty milliseconds; one in twenty misses a cache; one in two hundred falls into a heavy tail. <bookmark mark='a'/> The mean is thirty milliseconds, a latency almost no request has. <bookmark mark='b'/> The median, twenty and a half, is what a typical request sees. <bookmark mark='c'/> The ninety-ninth percentile is a hundred and seventy-seven, the ninety-nine point ninth eight hundred and thirty-four, and the slowest took a hundred and four seconds. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the tail is not rare for users: a page making a hundred requests meets one beyond the ninety-ninth percentile sixty-three times in a hundred, as Dean and Barroso pointed out.
145088f8ee45.zh: 这是20万个模拟的延迟，画在对数坐标轴上。大多数大约需要20毫秒；每20个中有1个缓存未命中；每200个中有1个落入重尾。<bookmark mark='a'/>平均值是30毫秒，这是几乎没有哪个请求会有的延迟。<bookmark mark='b'/>中位数是20.5毫秒，是一个典型请求看到的延迟。<bookmark mark='c'/>第99百分位数是177毫秒，第99.9百分位数是834毫秒，而最慢的那个用了104秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>而且对用户来说，尾部并不罕见：一个发出100个请求的页面，每100次中有63次会碰上一个超过第99百分位数的请求，正如 Dean 和 Barroso 指出的那样。

12a306e89ed8.en: Now ten servers, one of them four times slower than the rest. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each reports its ninety-ninth percentile: about a hundred and seventy-five milliseconds for nine, seven hundred and nineteen for the slow one. <bookmark mark='b'/> A dashboard that averages them shows two hundred and thirty. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the true ninety-ninth percentile of the fleet's requests is two hundred and seventy. Percentiles do not average. <bookmark mark='d'/> Distributions do combine: add the servers' histograms bucket by bucket, then read the quantile: two hundred and sixty-eight, within the sketch's one percent.
12a306e89ed8.zh: 现在有10台服务器，其中一台比其他的慢4倍。<bookmark mark='a'/>每台报告自己的第99百分位数：9台大约是175毫秒，慢的那台是719毫秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>一块把它们取平均的仪表盘显示230毫秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>但整个机群所有请求真正的第99百分位数是270毫秒。百分位数不能取平均。<bookmark mark='d'/>分布却能合并：把各台服务器的直方图逐桶相加，再读出分位数：268毫秒，在草图百分之1的误差之内。

ab500756403e.en: In 2019 Charles Masson, Jee Rim and Homin Lee, at Datadog, published a sketch with a guarantee, DDSketch. <bookmark mark='a'/> Choose a relative accuracy, alpha. Bucket boundaries are powers of gamma, one plus alpha over one minus alpha, so the buckets grow geometrically. <bookmark mark='b'/> To answer a quantile, find the bucket holding that rank and return two gamma to the i over gamma plus one. <bookmark mark='c'/> For any value in that bucket, the answer divided by the value lies between one minus alpha and one plus alpha. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the error is relative: one percent of a twenty-millisecond median, and one percent of a two-second tail. <bookmark mark='e'/> At one percent, these latencies fill three hundred and thirty-two buckets, and sketches merge by adding counts.
ab500756403e.zh: 2019年，Datadog 的 Charles Masson、Jee Rim 和 Homin Lee 发表了一种带保证的草图，DDSketch。<bookmark mark='a'/>选定一个相对精度 alpha。桶的边界是 gamma 的幂，gamma 等于1加 alpha，除以1减 alpha，所以桶按几何级数增长。<bookmark mark='b'/>要回答一个分位数，就找到包含那个秩的桶，返回2乘以 gamma 的 i 次方，再除以 gamma 加1。<bookmark mark='c'/>对那个桶里的任何值，答案除以这个值，都落在1减 alpha 和1加 alpha 之间。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以误差是相对的：是20毫秒中位数的百分之1，也是2秒尾部的百分之1。<bookmark mark='e'/>在百分之1的精度下，这些延迟填满了332个桶，而草图通过把计数相加来合并。

d92e172735ff.en: Four summaries of the same latencies. <bookmark mark='a'/> DDSketch stays within its one percent everywhere. The log-linear layout of Gil Tene's HdrHistogram, each power of two split into a hundred and twenty-eight parts, does better still, with three times the buckets. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 46's KLL is accurate at the median, but off by almost half at the ninety-nine point ninth percentile: it bounds the error in rank, and in a heavy tail neighbouring ranks are far apart in value. <bookmark mark='c'/> A random sample of a thousand holds almost none of the tail.
d92e172735ff.zh: 同一批延迟的四种概括。<bookmark mark='a'/>DDSketch 在各处都保持在它的百分之1以内。Gil Tene 的 HdrHistogram 采用对数线性布局，把每个2的幂分成128份，做得还要更好，用的桶是它的3倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>第46部分的 KLL 在中位数处很准确，但在第99.9百分位数处偏差将近一半：它界定的是秩上的误差，而在重尾里，相邻的秩在数值上相距很远。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个1000个元素的随机样本，几乎完全没有包含尾部。

fe2e78f2ae69.en: One more cost. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every distinct combination of label values is a separate time series, stored and indexed on its own. <bookmark mark='b'/> Five methods, eight status codes, forty routes and two hundred instances make three hundred and twenty thousand series for one metric. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add a user identifier, for a million users, and it becomes three hundred and twenty billion. <bookmark mark='d'/> So keep label values few and bounded; detail about single requests belongs in logs and traces, the next chapter.
fe2e78f2ae69.zh: 还有一项代价。<bookmark mark='a'/>标签值的每一种不同组合，都是一条单独的时间序列，单独存储，单独索引。<bookmark mark='b'/>5种请求方法、8种状态码、40条路由和200个实例，让一个指标产生32万条序列。<bookmark mark='c'/>再加上一个用户标识符，有100万个用户，它就变成了3200亿条。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以要让标签值少而有界；关于单个请求的细节，属于日志和追踪，也就是下一章。

ca7a5844bb38.en: Chapter eight. Logs and traces: following one request through many services.
ca7a5844bb38.zh: 第八章：日志与追踪：跟随一个请求穿过许多服务。

46d0a9ad433c.en: Logs come first. <bookmark mark='a'/> A line of prose is easy to write and hard to use. To count failures by route, someone writes a regular expression, and it breaks the day the message is reworded. <bookmark mark='b'/> A structured log writes the same event as named fields. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then questions become queries over Part 46's append-only streams: errors by route and region, counted, with their ninety-ninth percentile. <bookmark mark='d'/> One field matters most: the trace identifier. It joins every line that one request wrote, in every service it touched.
46d0a9ad433c.zh: 先说日志。<bookmark mark='a'/>一行散文式的文字容易写，却难以使用。要按路由统计失败，就得有人写一个正则表达式，而消息的措辞一改，它就坏了。<bookmark mark='b'/>结构化日志把同样的事件写成一些命名的字段。<bookmark mark='c'/>这样，问题就变成了对第46部分只追加的流的查询：按路由和区域统计错误，并给出它们的第99百分位数。<bookmark mark='d'/>有一个字段最重要：追踪标识符。它把一个请求在它触及的每一个服务里写下的每一行都连接起来。

158e4848b938.en: In 2010 Benjamin Sigelman and colleagues described Dapper, Google's tracing system. <bookmark mark='a'/> One user request crosses many services, and each unit of work becomes a span: a name, a start and an end, and three identifiers. <bookmark mark='b'/> The trace identifier is shared by every span of the request. The span identifier is the span's own. The parent identifier names the span that caused it, so the spans form a tree. <bookmark mark='c'/> The identifiers travel with the request in a header, which the W3C's Trace Context standard calls traceparent. Each service reads it, starts a child span, and passes the header on. <bookmark mark='d'/> Spans are reported separately and joined later by trace identifier. OpenTelemetry, formed in 2019, is today's common toolkit for all of this.
158e4848b938.zh: 2010年，Benjamin Sigelman 和同事描述了 Google 的追踪系统 Dapper。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个用户请求穿过许多服务，而每个工作单元都成为一个跨度（span）：一个名字、一个开始和一个结束，以及三个标识符。<bookmark mark='b'/>追踪标识符由这个请求的每个跨度共享。跨度标识符是这个跨度自己的。父标识符指明引起它的那个跨度，所以这些跨度构成一棵树。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些标识符放在一个请求头里，随请求一起传递，W3C 的 Trace Context 标准把这个头叫作 traceparent。每个服务读取它，开始一个子跨度，再把这个头传下去。<bookmark mark='d'/>跨度被分别上报，之后再按追踪标识符连接起来。2019年成立的 OpenTelemetry，是今天做这一切的通用工具包。

70e19c1d61a0.en: Here is one trace from our simulator, drawn as a waterfall: time runs to the right, and each span is indented under its parent. <bookmark mark='a'/> The front end starts, and checks authentication first. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then it calls the catalog and the recommender at the same time, and each calls its own dependencies in turn: a cache and then a database; features, and then a model. <bookmark mark='c'/> When both have answered, it renders the page. The whole request took thirty-two point six milliseconds. <bookmark mark='d'/> If it has to be faster, where should the effort go?
70e19c1d61a0.zh: 这是我们的模拟器生成的一条追踪，画成瀑布图：时间向右延伸，每个跨度缩进在它的父跨度下面。<bookmark mark='a'/>前端开始，先检查身份认证。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后它同时调用商品目录和推荐系统，而它们各自又依次调用自己的依赖项：一个缓存，然后一个数据库；特征，然后一个模型。<bookmark mark='c'/>两者都回答之后，它渲染页面。整个请求用了32.6毫秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果它必须更快，力气应该花在哪里？

9cc92ef09c2b.en: The answer is the critical path: the chain of work the end was waiting for. <bookmark mark='a'/> Walk back from the end: the front end waited for render, render for the recommender, the recommender for its model, the model for the features, and so back to authentication. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is the longest path through the DAG of the trace's work, as in Part 19. Along it the model accounts for twelve point six milliseconds, render for six, the features for five point eight. <bookmark mark='c'/> The catalog and its database are not on it. The database takes twelve and a half milliseconds, yet making it faster would save nothing. The catalog has seven point three milliseconds of slack: shave more than that off the model, and the catalog becomes critical instead.
9cc92ef09c2b.zh: 答案是关键路径：结束时刻一直在等待的那条工作链。<bookmark mark='a'/>从结束处往回走：前端在等渲染，渲染在等推荐系统，推荐系统在等它的模型，模型在等特征，就这样一路回到身份认证。<bookmark mark='b'/>它是这条追踪的工作所构成的有向无环图中的最长路径，就像在第19部分里那样。沿着它，模型占12.6毫秒，渲染占6毫秒，特征占5.8毫秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>商品目录和它的数据库不在这条路径上。数据库要花12.5毫秒，然而让它变快什么也省不下。商品目录有7.3毫秒的松弛时间：从模型上削掉比这更多的时间，商品目录就会反过来成为关键。

88a24f56c751.en: Tracing every request costs too much, so traces are sampled. <bookmark mark='a'/> Head sampling decides at the first span, with a coin that keeps one trace in a hundred, and the decision travels in the context, so every service keeps the same traces. Of fifty thousand simulated requests it kept five hundred and thirty-three, <bookmark mark='b'/> but only four of the eight hundred and seventy-six that failed, and fifty-four of the four thousand three hundred slow ones. <bookmark mark='c'/> Tail sampling decides when the trace has finished: keep every error, every trace over a hundred milliseconds, and one in a hundred of the rest. That kept all of them, in five thousand five hundred and eighty-four traces. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price: every span is buffered until its trace ends, at one collector chosen by hashing the trace identifier, Part 39 again.
88a24f56c751.zh: 追踪每个请求代价太高，所以要对追踪采样。<bookmark mark='a'/>头部采样在第一个跨度就做出决定，用一枚每100条追踪保留1条的硬币，而这个决定随上下文传递，所以每个服务保留的是同样的追踪。在5万个模拟请求中，它保留了533条，<bookmark mark='b'/>但在失败的876个请求中只保留了4条，在4300个慢请求中只保留了54条。<bookmark mark='c'/>尾部采样在追踪结束时才做决定：保留每一个错误、每一条超过100毫秒的追踪，以及其余追踪中的百分之1。这样就把它们全都保留了下来，一共5584条追踪。<bookmark mark='d'/>代价是：每个跨度都要缓存起来，直到它的追踪结束，缓存在一个通过对追踪标识符做哈希来选出的收集器上，又是第39部分。

cfbc43c2fbbc.en: Chapter nine. Coordinated omission: how a load test can hide the very tail it was built to measure.
cfbc43c2fbbc.zh: 第九章：协调遗漏：一次负载测试，怎样把它本来要测量的那个尾部藏起来。

e7c59ff7c507.en: Here is a load test. <bookmark mark='a'/> A generator is meant to send a hundred requests a second to a server that answers in one millisecond, except that every forty seconds the server freezes for four, as in a long garbage-collection pause. <bookmark mark='b'/> The generator is a closed loop: it sends a request, waits for the answer, then sends the next. <bookmark mark='c'/> When the server freezes, one request waits four seconds, and that is one sample. <bookmark mark='d'/> But in those four seconds the generator should have sent four hundred requests. Waiting, it sent none of them, so none were measured. The generator has coordinated with the server, against the measurement. <bookmark mark='e'/> Over two hundred seconds, twenty thousand requests were due, and eighteen thousand and five were recorded. The nineteen hundred and ninety-five skipped are exactly the ones that would have waited.
e7c59ff7c507.zh: 这是一次负载测试。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个生成器本应每秒向一台服务器发送100个请求，这台服务器在1毫秒内回答，只不过每隔40秒，它会冻结4秒，就像一次长时间的垃圾回收暂停。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个生成器是一个闭环：它发送一个请求，等待回答，然后发送下一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>当服务器冻结时，一个请求等了4秒，而那只是一个样本。<bookmark mark='d'/>但在那4秒里，生成器本应发送400个请求。它在等待，一个都没有发送，所以一个都没有被测量。生成器与服务器协调了起来，共同对付这次测量。<bookmark mark='e'/>在200秒里，本应发出2万个请求，记录下来的是1万8005个。被跳过的那1995个，恰恰就是本来会等待的那些。

db7dde31002b.en: Compare what the generator reported with the truth, measured from when each request should have been sent. <bookmark mark='a'/> The closed loop says the median is one millisecond, and so are the ninetieth, the ninety-ninth and even the ninety-nine point ninth percentiles. Only the maximum, four seconds, hints at trouble, and a maximum is easy to dismiss as a fluke. <bookmark mark='b'/> But the server was frozen a tenth of the time, so about a tenth of the requests due had to wait. The true ninetieth percentile is four hundred milliseconds; the ninety-ninth, three point six seconds. <bookmark mark='c'/> Even the mean is a hundred times larger: two hundred and twenty-three milliseconds, against two. A team reading the first column would ship a service whose users wait seconds.
db7dde31002b.zh: 把生成器报告的结果与真相比较，真相是从每个请求本应被发送的时刻开始测量的。<bookmark mark='a'/>闭环说中位数是1毫秒，第90、第99，甚至第99.9百分位数也都是。只有最大值，4秒，暗示了问题，而最大值很容易被当作偶然现象而忽略。<bookmark mark='b'/>但服务器有十分之一的时间处于冻结状态，所以本应发出的请求中，大约十分之一不得不等待。真正的第90百分位数是400毫秒；第99百分位数是3.6秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>就连平均值也大了100倍：223毫秒，对2毫秒。一个只读第一列的团队，会交付一个让用户等上好几秒的服务。

a77a89d8dcff.en: Look at one freeze through the requests' eyes. <bookmark mark='a'/> The closed loop has a single point: one request that waited four seconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> A request due a second into the freeze waits about three; one due near the end waits a moment, and then the backlog drains at a millisecond each. The true waits form a ramp from four seconds down to one millisecond, and the red area is what the test never saw. <bookmark mark='c'/> Gil Tene, of Azul Systems, named this coordinated omission. <bookmark mark='d'/> The cure is to send at fixed times, whether or not the last reply has arrived, an open loop, as his load generator wrk2 does; or else to charge every sample from its intended start time, a correction his HdrHistogram library can apply.
a77a89d8dcff.zh: 从请求的视角来看一次冻结。<bookmark mark='a'/>闭环只有一个点：一个等了4秒的请求。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个在冻结开始1秒后本应发出的请求，要等大约3秒；一个在快结束时本应发出的请求只等一会儿，然后积压的请求以每个1毫秒的速度排空。真实的等待时间构成一道斜坡，从4秒降到1毫秒，而红色区域就是这次测试从未看到的部分。<bookmark mark='c'/>Azul Systems 的 Gil Tene 把这称为协调遗漏。<bookmark mark='d'/>解药是在固定的时刻发送，不管上一个回复到没到，也就是开环，就像他的负载生成器 wrk2 那样；或者从每个样本预定的开始时间来计算它，这是他的 HdrHistogram 库可以做的一种校正。

916c0555f24a.en: The deeper lesson is about the shape of the load. In 2006 Bianca Schroeder, Adam Wierman and Mor Harchol-Balter called their paper on it a cautionary tale. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a closed system, a fixed number of users each think for a second, send one request, and wait for it. Response time stays bounded, because when the server slows, the users wait instead of sending, as our generator did. <bookmark mark='b'/> In an open system, requests arrive whatever happens, and Part 31's queue gives the response time at the same throughput. <bookmark mark='c'/> At ninety-two percent busy, the closed system answers in eighty-two milliseconds and the open one in a hundred and thirty-two. At full load the closed mean is half a second, while the open queue grows without limit. <bookmark mark='d'/> A web service faces many independent users, which is close to open. Test it with a closed loop, and you measure a gentler world than the one it lives in.
916c0555f24a.zh: 更深的教训在于负载的形态。2006年，Bianca Schroeder、Adam Wierman 和 Mor Harchol-Balter 把他们关于这个问题的论文称为一个警世故事。<bookmark mark='a'/>在封闭系统中，固定数量的用户每人思考1秒，发送一个请求，然后等待它。响应时间保持有界，因为当服务器变慢时，用户就等待而不是发送，正如我们的生成器那样。<bookmark mark='b'/>在开放系统中，无论发生什么，请求都会到达，而第31部分的队列给出了同样吞吐量下的响应时间。<bookmark mark='c'/>在百分之92的忙碌程度下，封闭系统在82毫秒内回答，开放系统在132毫秒内回答。在满负载下，封闭系统的平均值是半秒，而开放系统的队列无限增长。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个网络服务面对的是许多独立的用户，接近开放系统。用闭环去测试它，你测到的是一个比它所处的世界更温和的世界。

94cd1f0f0e62.en: Chapter ten. Profiling: finding where the time goes, and drawing it as a flame graph.
94cd1f0f0e62.zh: 第十章：性能剖析：找出时间花在哪里，并把它画成火焰图。

f2b6a8af0250.en: A sampling profiler does not trace every step. Now and then it interrupts the program and asks where it is. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pebble runs version zero of the Job over twenty thousand bytes of a novel: six point three million instructions. Every nine hundred and ninety-seventh, a prime, so that it cannot fall into step with a loop, the profiler reads the program counter. <bookmark mark='b'/> It maps the address to its routine, and the routine to its callers: main, then word, then scan. <bookmark mark='c'/> Counting the stacks gives a folded profile of six thousand three hundred and eleven samples, more than four in five of them in scan and next, the loop that walks the table.
f2b6a8af0250.zh: 采样剖析器并不跟踪每一步。它时不时地打断程序，问它在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>Pebble 在一部小说的2万个字节上运行那项任务的第0版：630万条指令。每到第997条指令，剖析器就读一次程序计数器，997是一个素数，这样它就不会和某个循环同步。<bookmark mark='b'/>它把这个地址映射到它所在的例程，再把这个例程映射到它的调用者：main，然后是 word，然后是 scan。<bookmark mark='c'/>统计这些栈，就得到一份包含6311个样本的折叠剖析数据，其中超过五分之四落在 scan 和 next 里，也就是遍历那张表的循环。

9f1b544049a5.en: How far can a count of samples be trusted? <bookmark mark='a'/> Each sample lands in a routine with some probability p, so the count is binomial: a share from n samples has a standard error of the square root of p times one minus p, over n. <bookmark mark='b'/> The emulator also counts every instruction exactly. Scan is sampled at forty-two point eight percent, give or take zero point six; exactly, it is forty-three point five. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every row but one misses by two standard errors or fewer, and that one by just over two, about what a binomial gives across this many rows. <bookmark mark='d'/> The error shrinks only as one over the square root of n: four times the samples to halve it. And a routine below one sample's worth of time can vanish: the digit printer ran nearly fourteen hundred instructions, and was never sampled.
9f1b544049a5.zh: 一组样本计数有多可信？<bookmark mark='a'/>每个样本以某个概率 p 落在一个例程里，所以计数服从二项分布：从 n 个样本得到的一个份额，其标准误差是 p 乘以1减 p、再除以 n 的平方根。<bookmark mark='b'/>模拟器还精确地统计了每一条指令。scan 的采样结果是百分之42.8，上下浮动0.6；精确值是百分之43.5。<bookmark mark='c'/>除了一行之外，每一行的偏差都不超过两个标准误差，而那一行也只是略超过两个，这大约正是二项分布在这么多行上会给出的结果。<bookmark mark='d'/>误差只按 n 的平方根分之一缩小：要让它减半，样本得多4倍。而一个耗时不到一个样本的例程可能会消失：打印数字的例程运行了将近1400条指令，却从来没有被采样到。

8061d5a432a3.en: In 2011 Brendan Gregg found a way to see a profile at a glance: the flame graph. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each box is a frame, as wide as the share of samples with that frame on the stack. <bookmark mark='b'/> Callers sit below their callees, so the top edge is where the processor actually was. <bookmark mark='c'/> Left to right is alphabetical, not time, so identical stacks merge. <bookmark mark='d'/> Read ours from the bottom. Word takes ninety-four and a half percent of all samples. Above it, scan and next take eighty-two, and cmp, comparing letters, most of the rest. The Job walks its table, entry by entry, for every word. <bookmark mark='e'/> The profile does not say make this loop faster. It says do not loop: Part 17's hash table finds a word in one probe.
8061d5a432a3.zh: 2011年，Brendan Gregg 找到了一种一眼看清剖析数据的方法：火焰图。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个方框是一个栈帧，它的宽度等于栈上有这个栈帧的样本所占的份额。<bookmark mark='b'/>调用者位于被调用者的下方，所以顶部边缘就是处理器实际所在的位置。<bookmark mark='c'/>从左到右是按字母顺序，而不是按时间，所以相同的栈会合并。<bookmark mark='d'/>从底部开始读我们的图。word 占全部样本的百分之94.5。在它上面，scan 和 next 占百分之82，而比较字母的 cmp 占了其余的大部分。那项任务对每一个词，都要逐项遍历它的表。<bookmark mark='e'/>剖析数据并没有说让这个循环更快。它说的是不要循环：第17部分的哈希表一次探查就能找到一个词。

be995492bb0e.en: The same idea works one layer down. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here a timer signal, firing a thousand times a second of processor time, samples the Python stack of the emulator itself. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sixty percent of the samples are in step: fetching, dispatching and executing each instruction in Python. Memory loads take fifteen percent, and the cache of decoded instructions twelve. <bookmark mark='c'/> The guest profile told the Job's author to change the algorithm. This one tells the emulator's author where the interpreter is slow.
be995492bb0e.zh: 同样的思想在下一层也行得通。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里，一个按处理器时间每秒触发1000次的定时器信号，对模拟器本身的 Python 栈进行采样。<bookmark mark='b'/>百分之60的样本落在 step 里：用 Python 取出、分派并执行每一条指令。内存读取占百分之15，已译码指令的缓存占百分之12。<bookmark mark='c'/>客户程序的剖析数据告诉那项任务的作者去改变算法。这一份则告诉模拟器的作者，解释器慢在哪里。

27d410d8f5ed.en: A profiler that samples the processor sees only time spent running. <bookmark mark='a'/> Real requests also wait: for a disk, a lock, a reply from the network. <bookmark mark='b'/> Timer samples land only where the thread was running, so a request stuck behind a lock can look idle. <bookmark mark='c'/> Off-CPU analysis catches the rest. Each time the scheduler switches a thread out, record its stack, and when it runs again, charge the time away to that stack. On-CPU plus off-CPU is wall-clock time. <bookmark mark='d'/> eBPF, from Part 31, makes this cheap: a small verified program on the scheduler's tracepoint sums the waits inside the kernel, and only the totals reach user space.
27d410d8f5ed.zh: 一个对处理器采样的剖析器，只能看到花在运行上的时间。<bookmark mark='a'/>真实的请求还会等待：等磁盘、等锁、等来自网络的回复。<bookmark mark='b'/>定时器样本只落在线程正在运行的地方，所以一个卡在锁后面的请求，看起来可能是空闲的。<bookmark mark='c'/>离 CPU（off-CPU）分析能抓住其余的部分。每当调度器把一个线程换出，就记录下它的栈，而当它再次运行时，把离开的这段时间记到那个栈上。在 CPU 上的时间加上离开 CPU 的时间，就是墙上时钟时间。<bookmark mark='d'/>第31部分的 eBPF 让这件事变得很便宜：一个挂在调度器跟踪点上、经过验证的小程序，在内核里把等待时间加总，只有总数才会到达用户空间。

daef8219090a.en: Chapter eleven. Performance as a method: where to look first, how much capacity to buy, and how to notice when things get slower.
daef8219090a.zh: 第十一章：作为方法的性能：先看哪里，买多少容量，以及怎样注意到系统变慢了。

0b1fd3359b4b.en: Faced with a slow system, the worst method is to look wherever you happen to know the tools. <bookmark mark='a'/> Brendan Gregg's USE method is a checklist instead. For every resource, the processors, memory, disks and network, check utilisation, the share of time it was busy; saturation, the work queued that it cannot take yet; and errors. <bookmark mark='b'/> Going down the list finds what the eye misses. Here the disk is only sixty percent busy, yet requests queue for it in bursts. Saturation, not utilisation, was the clue. <bookmark mark='c'/> For services, Tom Wilkie's RED method asks for the rate of requests, the errors, and the duration, as a distribution, as chapter seven insisted. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google's site reliability book calls its version the four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and saturation.
0b1fd3359b4b.zh: 面对一个很慢的系统，最糟糕的方法是哪里的工具你碰巧熟悉，就去看哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>Brendan Gregg 的 USE 方法则是一份检查清单。对每一种资源，处理器、内存、磁盘和网络，检查利用率，也就是它忙碌的时间所占的比例；饱和度，也就是排着队、它还接不下的工作；以及错误。<bookmark mark='b'/>逐项检查清单，能发现眼睛漏掉的东西。这里磁盘只有百分之60的时间在忙，然而请求却一阵一阵地为它排队。线索是饱和度，而不是利用率。<bookmark mark='c'/>对于服务，Tom Wilkie 的 RED 方法要求看请求的速率、错误和持续时间，持续时间要看分布，正如第七章所坚持的那样。<bookmark mark='d'/>Google 的《站点可靠性工程》一书把它的版本称为四个黄金信号：延迟、流量、错误和饱和度。

1a8c0a253424.en: For code that computes, the first question is which resource is the limit, and Part 9's roofline answers it on one chart. <bookmark mark='a'/> Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman and David Patterson drew it in 2009. Across, the arithmetic a kernel does per byte it fetches from memory; up, the operations per second it can reach. Two roofs cap it: the slope of memory bandwidth, and the flat line of peak arithmetic. <bookmark mark='b'/> A table scan does little arithmetic per byte and sits under the slope. A faster processor buys it nothing; moving fewer bytes, with Part 9's caches and tiles, buys everything. <bookmark mark='c'/> A tiled matrix multiply sits under the flat roof, where only more arithmetic helps, the territory of AI, Built's Part 17 accelerators. Measure first where a program sits, then decide what to change.
1a8c0a253424.zh: 对于做计算的代码，第一个问题是哪种资源是限制，而第9部分的屋顶线模型在一张图上回答了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>Samuel Williams、Andrew Waterman 和 David Patterson 在2009年画出了它。横轴是一个内核从内存每取一个字节所做的运算量；纵轴是它能达到的每秒运算次数。有两道屋顶给它封顶：内存带宽的斜坡，和峰值运算能力的平线。<bookmark mark='b'/>一次表扫描每个字节只做很少的运算，位于斜坡之下。更快的处理器对它毫无帮助；用第9部分的缓存和分块来搬运更少的字节，才是一切。<bookmark mark='c'/>分块矩阵乘法位于平坦的屋顶之下，在那里只有更多的运算能力才有帮助，那是《人工智能，从零搭建》第17部分的加速器的领地。先测量一个程序位于哪里，再决定要改变什么。

0825289dde38.en: Capacity planning asks how many servers next year's load will need, and queueing theory answers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each book takes the Job's service eighty milliseconds, and we want the mean wait under twenty milliseconds, with at most one request in five waiting at all. <bookmark mark='b'/> At twelve books a second, about one server's worth of work, Erlang's formula from Part 45 asks for three servers, only thirty-two percent busy. At a thousand a second it asks for ninety, eighty-nine percent busy. <bookmark mark='c'/> Bigger pools run hotter for the same wait, because the spare capacity they need grows only like the square root of the load: two spare servers at the top of the table, ten at the bottom. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then add chapter six's spares for failures, and check the plan with an open-loop load test, or chapter nine's illusion will flatter it.
0825289dde38.zh: 容量规划问的是，明年的负载需要多少台服务器，而排队论给出了回答。<bookmark mark='a'/>那项任务的服务处理每本书要80毫秒，而我们希望平均等待时间低于20毫秒，并且最多每5个请求中有1个需要等待。<bookmark mark='b'/>每秒12本书，大约是一台服务器的工作量，第45部分的 Erlang 公式要求3台服务器，忙碌程度只有百分之32。每秒1000本时，它要求90台，百分之89忙碌。<bookmark mark='c'/>在同样的等待时间下，更大的服务器池能跑得更满，因为它们需要的备用容量只按负载的平方根增长：表格顶部多出2台备用服务器，底部多出10台。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后再加上第六章为应对故障而准备的备用，并用一次开环负载测试来检验这份计划，否则第九章的那种错觉会美化它。

45a33739e11a.en: Last, regressions. A team wants to know the day its code got slower, not the month. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are eighty commits, each benchmarked once. Runs vary by about two percent, and from commit fifty-two on, the code is three percent slower. <bookmark mark='b'/> A naive rule alerts whenever a run is five percent slower than the one before. It fires five times. Four are noise, and the real one looks no different from them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Change-point detection asks where one split would best separate the series into two different means. It answers commit fifty-two: from one point zero zero zero to one point zero three two. <bookmark mark='d'/> Is that luck? Shuffle the measurements and search again. In two thousand shuffles, none split as well. MongoDB's engineers described running tests of this kind on their benchmarks in continuous integration in 2020.
45a33739e11a.zh: 最后是性能回退。一个团队想知道它的代码是哪一天变慢的，而不是哪个月。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有80次提交，每次都运行一遍基准测试。每次运行的波动大约是百分之2，而从第52次提交起，代码慢了百分之3。<bookmark mark='b'/>一条朴素的规则，只要某次运行比上一次慢百分之5，就发出告警。它触发了5次。其中4次是噪声，而真正的那一次看起来和它们没有任何区别。<bookmark mark='c'/>变点检测问的是，在哪里做一次切分，能最好地把这个序列分成均值不同的两段。它的回答是第52次提交：从1.000到1.032。<bookmark mark='d'/>那是运气吗？把测量值打乱，再搜索一遍。在2000次打乱中，没有一次切分得这么好。MongoDB 的工程师在2020年描述了在持续集成中对他们的基准测试运行这类检验。

4dc662b7478b.en: Chapter twelve. Incidents: what people do while a system is broken, and what they learn afterwards.
4dc662b7478b.zh: 第十二章：事故：系统坏掉时人们做些什么，以及他们事后学到了什么。

5aa2721c9fc1.en: Here is an incident, as it typically unfolds. <bookmark mark='a'/> A change ships, and two minutes later errors begin. Google's site reliability book reports that about seventy percent of its outages came from changes to a live system. <bookmark mark='b'/> Chapter two's fast-burn alert pages the on-call engineer, who acknowledges, sees users affected, and declares an incident: now one named person is in charge, and customers are told. <bookmark mark='c'/> The first goal is not to understand the bug but to stop the harm, usually by undoing the change. Here the rollback ends it at minute thirty-four. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two intervals are tracked across incidents: the time to detect, and the time to mitigate. The root cause can wait for the next day, when nobody is in a hurry.
5aa2721c9fc1.zh: 这是一次事故，它通常是这样展开的。<bookmark mark='a'/>一项变更上线，两分钟后错误开始出现。Google 的《站点可靠性工程》一书报告说，它大约百分之70的中断来自对线上系统的变更。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二章的快速消耗告警呼叫值班工程师，他确认告警，看到用户受到了影响，于是宣布进入事故状态：现在由一个指定的人负责，并且通知客户。<bookmark mark='c'/>首要目标不是弄懂这个缺陷，而是止住伤害，通常的办法是撤销那项变更。这里，回滚在第34分钟结束了它。<bookmark mark='d'/>跨事故追踪的有两个时间间隔：检测时间和缓解时间。根本原因可以等到第二天，那时谁都不着急。

3fc1c5b50ef6.en: The roles come from firefighting: Google's book adapts the Incident Command System, developed by American wildfire crews in the 1970s. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the centre, the incident commander holds the whole picture, decides and assigns work, and deliberately does not debug. <bookmark mark='b'/> The operations lead is the only one changing the system, so that two people never fight over it. <bookmark mark='c'/> The communication lead updates the status page and stakeholders on a fixed schedule, so that nobody interrupts the operators to ask. Planning keeps the log of what was tried, and arranges hand-offs. <bookmark mark='d'/> The roles are hats, not ranks: in a small incident one person wears several.
3fc1c5b50ef6.zh: 这些角色来自消防：Google 的那本书改编了事故指挥系统（Incident Command System），它是美国的野火扑救队伍在20世纪70年代发展出来的。<bookmark mark='a'/>处在中心的是事故指挥官，他掌握全局，做出决定，分派工作，而且刻意不去调试。<bookmark mark='b'/>运维负责人是唯一改动系统的人，这样就不会有两个人争夺它。<bookmark mark='c'/>沟通负责人按固定的时间表更新状态页，并通知相关方，这样就没有人去打断操作人员来询问。计划负责人记录尝试过什么，并安排交接。<bookmark mark='d'/>这些角色是帽子，而不是军衔：在一次小事故里，一个人会戴好几顶。

0bf2393c7508.en: Afterwards comes the post-mortem: a written account of what happened and what will change. <bookmark mark='a'/> Google's template has a summary; the impact, in users, minutes and error budget; a timeline; contributing factors; what went well and what went wrong; <bookmark mark='b'/> and a section many teams find the most useful: where we got lucky. <bookmark mark='c'/> It is written without blame. Punish the person who typed the command, and the next person hides their mistake, and the organisation stops learning. <bookmark mark='d'/> John Allspaw, writing about Etsy's practice in 2012, asked not who made the mistake but why the action made sense at the time, with what they knew then. <bookmark mark='e'/> And every action item gets an owner and a date.
0bf2393c7508.zh: 之后是事后复盘：一份书面记录，写明发生了什么，以及什么会改变。<bookmark mark='a'/>Google 的模板包含一份摘要；影响，以用户数、分钟数和错误预算来计；一条时间线；促成因素；哪些做得好，哪些出了错；<bookmark mark='b'/>还有一节许多团队认为最有用：我们在哪里走了运。<bookmark mark='c'/>它是不追责的。惩罚那个敲下命令的人，下一个人就会隐藏自己的错误，而组织就不再学习。<bookmark mark='d'/>John Allspaw 在2012年写到 Etsy 的做法时，问的不是谁犯了错，而是在当时、以他们当时所知道的，这个操作为什么显得合理。<bookmark mark='e'/>而每个行动项都有一个负责人和一个日期。

b70690d39e29.en: Why do incidents happen in systems built by careful people? James Reason, a psychologist who studied human error, offered a picture: the Swiss-cheese model. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every defence is a slice with holes in it, and the holes move. Harm gets through only when they line up. <bookmark mark='b'/> Take the S3 outage from the start of this part. The trigger was a mistyped input, but the tool also let too much capacity be removed, too quickly. <bookmark mark='c'/> The removed subsystems had not been fully restarted in the larger regions for years, so recovery was slow. And Amazon's status page could not at first show the problem, because it depended on S3. <bookmark mark='d'/> Four holes, lined up. Blaming the typist closes one.
b70690d39e29.zh: 为什么在细心的人建造的系统里还会发生事故？研究人为差错的心理学家 James Reason 给出了一幅图景：瑞士奶酪模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一道防御都是一片带孔的奶酪，而这些孔会移动。只有当它们排成一线时，伤害才能穿过去。<bookmark mark='b'/>拿这一部分开头的 S3 中断来说。触发因素是一个打错的输入，但那个工具也允许移除太多的容量，而且太快。<bookmark mark='c'/>被移除的子系统在较大的区域里已经好多年没有完整重启过了，所以恢复很慢。而 Amazon 的状态页起初无法显示这个问题，因为它本身依赖于 S3。<bookmark mark='d'/>四个孔，排成了一线。责怪打字的人，只堵上了其中一个。

66ef11d36865.en: In 1998 Richard Cook, a physician who studied safety in medicine, wrote a short paper called How Complex Systems Fail. <bookmark mark='a'/> Complex systems run in degraded mode, with something always broken somewhere. <bookmark mark='b'/> So catastrophe needs several failures at once: the Swiss cheese again. <bookmark mark='c'/> A single root cause is therefore a story told with hindsight, <bookmark mark='d'/> and hindsight makes every error look obvious. <bookmark mark='e'/> The people running a system are not its weak link but the adaptable part that creates its safety, mostly unseen. <bookmark mark='f'/> And every change, even a fix, introduces new forms of failure.
66ef11d36865.zh: 1998年，研究医疗安全的医生 Richard Cook 写了一篇短文，题为《复杂系统如何失败》（How Complex Systems Fail）。<bookmark mark='a'/>复杂系统在降级模式下运行，总有某处有某样东西是坏的。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以灾难需要几个故障同时发生：又是瑞士奶酪。<bookmark mark='c'/>因此，单一的根本原因，是一个借助事后之明讲出来的故事，<bookmark mark='d'/>而事后之明让每一个错误都显得显而易见。<bookmark mark='e'/>运行系统的人不是它的薄弱环节，而是创造出它的安全的那个善于适应的部分，而这大多不为人所见。<bookmark mark='f'/>而每一次变更，哪怕是一次修复，都会引入新的失败形式。

8d61b3c0160c.en: Chapter thirteen. Chaos engineering: breaking a system on purpose, before the world does it for you.
8d61b3c0160c.zh: 第十三章：混沌工程：在世界替你动手之前，故意破坏一个系统。

7ce74ccd85d9.en: When Netflix moved its streaming service onto Amazon's cloud, its engineers accepted that any machine could vanish at any moment, and decided to make sure their services believed it too. <bookmark mark='a'/> They wrote Chaos Monkey, a program that picks instances at random and terminates them, in production. <bookmark mark='b'/> It runs during working hours, when the engineers who must respond are at their desks. A service that cannot lose one machine is found out on a Tuesday afternoon, not at three in the morning. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2011 Netflix described a whole Simian Army. Latency Monkey added delays, and Chaos Gorilla took out an entire availability zone, so that traffic had to move to the others. Later, Chaos Kong drilled the evacuation of a whole region.
7ce74ccd85d9.zh: 当 Netflix 把它的流媒体服务迁到 Amazon 的云上时，它的工程师接受了任何机器都可能随时消失这一事实，并决定确保他们的服务也相信这一点。<bookmark mark='a'/>他们写了 Chaos Monkey，一个在生产环境里随机挑选实例并终止它们的程序。<bookmark mark='b'/>它在工作时间运行，那时必须做出响应的工程师都坐在工位上。一个经不起失去一台机器的服务，会在某个星期二的下午被发现，而不是在凌晨三点。<bookmark mark='c'/>2011年，Netflix 描述了一整支猿猴军团（Simian Army）。Latency Monkey 加入延迟，Chaos Gorilla 撤下整整一个可用区，迫使流量转移到其他可用区。后来，Chaos Kong 演练了整个区域的撤离。

b2aaf186b939.en: In 2016 Ali Basiri and his colleagues at Netflix set out the discipline as a scientific method. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, define the steady state: a measurable output that users feel, not an internal gauge. Netflix used the number of streams started per second. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second, state a hypothesis: that the steady state will be the same in an experiment group as in a control group. <bookmark mark='c'/> Third, inject the events the real world produces: machines crashing, networks partitioning, replies slowing, bad deployments, sudden load. <bookmark mark='d'/> Fourth, look for a difference between the two groups. If there is none, confidence grows. If there is one, you have found a weakness before your users did. <bookmark mark='e'/> And do it in production, because only production has production's traffic, and do it continuously, because the system changes every day.
b2aaf186b939.zh: 2016年，Netflix 的 Ali Basiri 和同事把这门学科阐述为一种科学方法。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一，定义稳态：一个用户能感受到的可测量的输出，而不是某个内部的计量值。Netflix 用的是每秒开始播放的流的数目。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二，提出一个假设：实验组中的稳态会与对照组中的稳态相同。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三，注入真实世界会产生的事件：机器崩溃、网络分区、回复变慢、糟糕的部署、突如其来的负载。<bookmark mark='d'/>第四，寻找两组之间的差异。如果没有差异，信心就增加。如果有差异，你就在用户之前发现了一个弱点。<bookmark mark='e'/>而且要在生产环境里做，因为只有生产环境才有生产环境的流量；还要持续地做，因为系统每天都在变。

a0f13f3ac3e1.en: Experimenting in production is responsible only if the damage is bounded, so the practitioners' published principles add a fifth rule: minimise the blast radius. <bookmark mark='a'/> Route a small slice of users, say one percent, to the experiment, and another one percent to a control group with no fault. Everyone else is untouched. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now crash one of the Job service's three replicas, under the naive client of chapter fourteen. The experiment group loses a third of its requests at once. <bookmark mark='c'/> An abort rule, written before the start, stops the experiment as soon as the group misses the objective for a minute. The dashed line is what it spared them. <bookmark mark='d'/> The experiment cost under a hundredth of a percent of the month's error budget. Unconfined, on all traffic for chapter fourteen's hour of faults, the same weakness costs thirteen percent. The hypothesis was refuted, cheaply.
a0f13f3ac3e1.zh: 只有当损害有界时，在生产环境里做实验才是负责任的，所以实践者公布的原则加上了第五条规则：把爆炸半径减到最小。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一小部分用户，比如百分之1，导向实验组，再把另外百分之1导向一个没有故障的对照组。其他所有人都不受影响。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在，在第十四章的那个朴素客户端下，让那项任务的服务的3个副本之一崩溃。实验组立刻失去了三分之一的请求。<bookmark mark='c'/>一条在开始前就写好的中止规则，一旦这个组有一分钟没有达到目标，就停止实验。虚线就是它为他们免去的损失。<bookmark mark='d'/>这次实验花掉的错误预算，不到这个月的万分之一。如果不加限制，在全部流量上经历第十四章那一小时的故障，同样的弱点要花掉百分之13。这个假设被推翻了，而且代价很小。

99d010dc202e.en: How is a fault injected? <bookmark mark='a'/> A crash is the easiest: kill the process, or terminate the machine, and connections are refused at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> A partition is a firewall rule that silently drops packets, so a caller hears nothing and must wait out its timeout. <bookmark mark='c'/> Slowness is added in the kernel's queueing layer by Linux's network emulator: chapter three's gray failure. Our simulator models all three. <bookmark mark='d'/> For Part 38's Raft cluster the hypotheses are stronger, because consensus promises more. Crash the leader: a new one within a few election timeouts, and nothing committed lost. Cut the leader off in a minority: it can commit nothing, while the majority carries on. Crash two of five followers: no pause at all. <bookmark mark='e'/> Written down before the run, each is a claim that can fail. Chapter fourteen runs both experiments.
99d010dc202e.zh: 故障是怎样注入的？<bookmark mark='a'/>崩溃是最容易的：杀死进程，或者终止机器，连接就会立刻被拒绝。<bookmark mark='b'/>网络分区是一条悄悄丢弃数据包的防火墙规则，所以调用者什么也听不到，只能等到它的超时。<bookmark mark='c'/>变慢则由 Linux 的网络模拟器在内核的排队层里加入：这就是第三章的灰色故障。我们的模拟器对这三种都做了建模。<bookmark mark='d'/>对于第38部分的 Raft 集群，假设要更强，因为共识承诺得更多。让领导者崩溃：在几个选举超时之内选出一个新的领导者，而且已提交的东西一样都不丢。把领导者隔离在少数派里：它什么都提交不了，而多数派照常运行。让5个节点中的两个跟随者崩溃：完全没有停顿。<bookmark mark='e'/>在运行之前写下来，每一个都是一个可能失败的断言。第十四章会运行这两个实验。

be2005941027.en: Chapter fourteen. The Job's service, broken on purpose.
be2005941027.zh: 第十四章：那项任务的服务，被故意破坏。

97679dfa041c.en: The Job's counting service runs as three replicas, and clients spread requests over them. <bookmark mark='a'/> A chaos experiment starts with a hypothesis about the steady state, stated in the terms the users care about: ninety-nine point nine percent of requests answered correctly within three hundred milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then, during one simulated hour, we break things. At minute ten the first counter crashes, and connections to it are refused at once. At minute twenty-five the second is cut off by a partition, so requests to it simply vanish. And at minute forty the third turns ten times slower, the gray failure that health checks often miss. <bookmark mark='c'/> We run the hour three times, with three clients: a naive one; one with a timeout and a single retry on another replica; and one that also ejects a replica after five failures in a row, and hedges a slow request after a hundred milliseconds.
97679dfa041c.zh: 那项任务的计数服务以3个副本运行，客户端把请求分散到它们上面。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次混沌实验从关于稳态的一个假设开始，用用户关心的语言来表述：百分之99.9的请求在300毫秒内得到正确的回答。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后，在模拟的一小时里，我们来破坏东西。第10分钟，第一个计数器崩溃，到它的连接立刻被拒绝。第25分钟，第二个被一次网络分区隔断，所以发往它的请求就这么消失了。而在第40分钟，第三个变慢了10倍，这是健康检查常常漏掉的灰色故障。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们用三种客户端把这一小时跑三遍：一个朴素的客户端；一个带有超时，并在另一个副本上重试一次的客户端；还有一个，在连续5次失败后还会剔除那个副本，并在100毫秒后对慢请求发出对冲。

485a56780f13.en: Here is the share of requests that met the objective, minute by minute. <bookmark mark='a'/> The naive client loses a third of its requests whenever a replica is crashed or cut off, since one request in three goes to it, and about 24 percent while one is slow. Over the hour it keeps 90.5 percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> A timeout and one retry elsewhere recover almost everything: 99.91 percent, just above the objective. The misses are requests that wait out the timeout and then meet a slow reply. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ejection and hedging close the gap: the sick replica leaves the rotation within seconds, and the few slow replies are raced by a copy. Not one request in the hour missed. The price is in the next chart.
485a56780f13.zh: 这是每分钟达到目标的请求所占的份额。<bookmark mark='a'/>每当一个副本崩溃或被隔断，朴素的客户端就失去三分之一的请求，因为每3个请求中有1个发往它；而在一个副本变慢时，失去大约百分之24。在这一小时里，它保住了百分之90.5。<bookmark mark='b'/>一次超时，再到别处重试一次，几乎挽回了一切：百分之99.91，刚好高于目标。没达标的，是那些等完超时、然后又碰上一个慢回复的请求。<bookmark mark='c'/>剔除和对冲补上了这个缺口：生病的副本在几秒之内就退出轮转，而少数几个慢回复则被一份拷贝赛过。这一小时里没有一个请求没达标。代价在下一张图里。

17bb5c4351df.en: Count the hour against the month's error budget, a tenth of a percent of a month of requests. <bookmark mark='a'/> The naive client burned 13 percent of the whole month's budget in one hour of faults. <bookmark mark='b'/> Retrying used 0.13 percent, at the price of 11 percent more requests, because every timed-out or refused request was sent twice. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ejection cut the retries, since the broken replica stopped receiving traffic, so the best client was also the cheaper of the two: 1.2 percent extra. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is what an error budget is for: it turns reliability from a feeling into a number you can spend, and lets you price each defence.
17bb5c4351df.zh: 把这一小时记到这个月的错误预算上，预算是一个月请求量的千分之一。<bookmark mark='a'/>朴素的客户端在一小时的故障里，烧掉了整个月预算的百分之13。<bookmark mark='b'/>重试用掉了百分之0.13，代价是多出百分之11的请求，因为每一个超时或被拒绝的请求都发送了两次。<bookmark mark='c'/>剔除减少了重试，因为坏掉的副本不再接收流量，所以最好的客户端也是两者中更便宜的那个：额外的请求只有百分之1.2。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是错误预算的用途：它把可靠性从一种感觉变成一个你可以花费的数字，并让你能给每一种防御定价。

177e1cd468c1.en: Chaos experiments are just as useful on consensus. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is Part 38's five-node Raft cluster taking twenty client commands a second, and the share of each second's commands that were eventually committed. <bookmark mark='b'/> When we crash the leader, there is a dip of a fraction of a second: the election timeout, then a vote. Cutting the leader off in a minority causes another. Crashing two followers costs nothing at all, because three of five is still a majority. <bookmark mark='c'/> And through all of it the safety checker found no violation: no committed command was ever lost or reordered. The cluster traded a little availability for consistency, exactly as Part 38 promised it would.
177e1cd468c1.zh: 混沌实验对共识同样有用。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是第38部分那个5节点的 Raft 集群，每秒接收20条客户端命令，以及每一秒的命令中最终被提交的份额。<bookmark mark='b'/>当我们让领导者崩溃时，会出现一个不到一秒的下凹：先是选举超时，然后是一次投票。把领导者隔离在少数派里，又造成一次下凹。让两个跟随者崩溃则毫无代价，因为5个中的3个仍然是多数派。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在整个过程中，安全性检查器没有发现任何违规：没有一条已提交的命令丢失或被重新排序。这个集群用一点点可用性换来了一致性，正如第38部分承诺的那样。

3db5217a5078.en: The ledger gets row nineteen, and for once the row is not about being faster. <bookmark mark='a'/> With one of the service's forty-two workers ten times slow, the thirty books take about 0.71 seconds without hedging, since one of them usually lands on the slow worker, and 0.30 seconds with a hedge after two hundred and forty milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> That is a shade faster than the healthy service without hedges, because a hedge also trims the ordinary tail, for about two extra requests in thirty. Reliability engineering rarely makes the good case faster. It keeps the bad case close to the good one, which is what users actually notice.
3db5217a5078.zh: 账本添上第19行，而这一次，这一行讲的不是更快。<bookmark mark='a'/>当服务的42个工作进程中有一个慢了10倍时，30本书在不对冲的情况下大约需要0.71秒，因为其中通常有一本会落到那个慢的工作进程上；而在240毫秒后发出对冲时，需要0.30秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>这比不带对冲的健康服务还要稍快一点，因为对冲也会修剪掉普通的尾部，代价是每30个请求大约多出2个。可靠性工程很少让好的情况变得更快。它让坏的情况保持接近好的情况，而这正是用户真正会注意到的。

2da771006a20.en: Chapter fifteen, the frontier. Can we predict the failures that persist?
2da771006a20.zh: 第十五章：前沿。我们能预测那些持续存在的故障吗？

d6e2660bb95b.en: The easy failures are the ones where something stops. <bookmark mark='a'/> The hard ones are gray: a replica whose health check answers OK, because the check is cheap and fast, <bookmark mark='b'/> while the users' real requests time out on a slow disk, a lossy link or a stuck thread. <bookmark mark='c'/> Peng Huang and colleagues named this in 2017, and called its cause differential observability: the failure detector and the application see different worlds. <bookmark mark='d'/> The remedy is to judge health the way users do, from the outcomes of real requests, as the Job's best client did when it ejected the slow replica.
d6e2660bb95b.zh: 容易的故障，是那些有某样东西停下来的故障。<bookmark mark='a'/>困难的故障是灰色的：一个副本的健康检查回答 OK，因为这个检查又便宜又快，<bookmark mark='b'/>而用户的真实请求却因为一块慢磁盘、一条丢包的链路或一个卡住的线程而超时。<bookmark mark='c'/>Peng Huang 和同事在2017年给它起了名字，并把它的原因称为差异可观测性：故障检测器和应用程序看到的是不同的世界。<bookmark mark='d'/>补救办法是像用户那样判断健康状况，根据真实请求的结果，正如那项任务最好的客户端剔除那个慢副本时所做的那样。

91b6ff0264de.en: Metastable failures are the frontier's sharpest problem.
